briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the climate briefing for October 21, 2026. Today, as warnings about the severity of climate change continue globally, significant developments and diverse efforts to address the climate crisis have been reported both domestically and internationally.

sections.title: 🔴 Global Climate Crisis Warnings and Deepening Concerns
sections.content: According to a UN report, global warming is projected to exceed 1.5°C, raising an urgent alarm for the achievement of the Paris Agreement goals [22, 166]. The UN Secretary-General warned that global climate action is 'dangerously inadequate,' specifically pointing to some responsibility on the part of the United States and emphasizing that the world is regressing in its efforts to curb climate change [156, 162, 163, 170]. In Europe, more than half of heatwave-related deaths have been linked to climate change, indicating that the direct human cost of the climate crisis is becoming a reality [164]. Furthermore, the UN Environment Programme (UNEP) stated that carbon emissions must be reduced by 18% within the next four years and nearly halved within ten years to avoid catastrophic climate target overshoots, but warned that the opportunity to achieve the 1.5°C warming limit 'without overshoot' has already been lost [175, 179]. In light of this situation, the UK government's decision to approve drilling at the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea has drawn strong criticism from climate activists [173, 174].

sections.title: 🌍 Strengthening International Cooperation and Domestic Carbon Neutrality Efforts
sections.content: South Korea is deepening its Green Partnership with the European Union (EU) for energy transition, environmental protection, and climate change response, discussing specific policy cooperation areas such as NDCs, emissions trading schemes, and offshore wind power [1, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 13, 15]. The EU is leading international climate action by finalizing its goal to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 90% by 2040 compared to 1990 levels [145]. Domestically, the 10th Carbon Neutrality International Conference opened in Chungcheongnam-do, where practical carbon neutrality measures between local governments and businesses were actively discussed, alongside the full-scale launch of Asia climate technology ODA cooperation [34, 40, 41, 45, 52, 54, 55, 62, 65, 70, 71, 75, 78, 91, 97, 98, 100, 106]. Vietnam is also actively responding to climate change by enhancing the transparency of greenhouse gas emission information and improving related systems, while also learning hydrogen production technology using renewable energy from Japan [19, 25, 26, 150].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and New Horizons
sections.content: Domestic renewable energy generation capacity has surpassed coal power generation capacity for the first time ever, becoming the second-largest power source in the country after LNG [110, 111, 112, 117, 118, 119, 121, 122, 123, 124, 125, 126, 132, 133, 134, 135]. This indicates that a significant shift in the power mix is underway, with projections suggesting that renewables could even overtake LNG within 2-3 years [119, 132]. Shinseong E&G is leading technological innovation by introducing AI data center cooling and renewable energy solutions [113, 130, 137], while various local governments and companies, including Goksung-gun, Western Power, and Gimhae City, are actively collaborating to expand renewable energy and achieve energy self-sufficient cities [114, 127, 143, 146, 148, 151]. Meanwhile, with the era of RPS (Renewable Portfolio Standard) coming to an end, companies are facing a major transformation in the renewable energy market, making the search for survival strategies crucial [115, 120, 140].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Climate Change Response: Challenges and Grassroots Initiatives
sections.content: Domestically, challenges and controversies surrounding climate change response persist, including a barrage of information disclosure requests for studies identifying responsibility for climate change, and concerns expressed over attempts to ease regulations on internal combustion engine vehicles [2, 4]. The emergency regarding heavy metals in a specific nation's drinking water sources [3] and the complete lack of performance by the National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives in advancing climate change response tasks [8] illustrate the direct impacts of climate change and the sluggishness of policy implementation. Meanwhile, research findings on the potential harmfulness of eco-friendly paper straws [21] call for a cautious approach to developing environmentally friendly products. Amidst these circumstances, local governments continue their proactive efforts, such as Gwangmyeong City's proposal for '100 Leading Local Governments for Carbon Neutrality' [28, 61, 66, 72, 104] and the opening of the Namyangju City Carbon Neutrality Support Center [29, 30, 48, 57, 67, 88, 107, 108]. Across the country, grassroots efforts are actively underway to strengthen citizens' climate crisis response capabilities and spread a culture of carbon neutrality through various educational programs and campaigns, including 'Visiting Carbon Neutrality Classrooms' [17, 93] and Carbon Neutrality Practice Competitions [36, 37, 80, 87, 99] [16, 18, 20, 24, 31, 32, 35, 38, 39, 42, 43, 46, 49, 50, 51, 53, 56, 58, 59, 60, 63, 64, 69, 73, 74, 76, 77, 79, 81, 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 89, 90, 92, 94, 95, 96, 101, 103, 105, 109, 153].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted global climate crisis warnings, alongside significant progress in international cooperation and renewable energy transition. Simultaneously, it has underscored the challenges that need to be addressed both domestically and internationally, as well as the importance of grassroots initiatives. This is a critical juncture that demands sustained attention and effort in responding to climate change. This concludes today's climate briefing.
